subject: RE: Urgent: Production incident — Hosted->Dedicated/Private decision & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finplus.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: capacity needs & hosted vs dedicated/private options

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap of the requirements you surfaced and next steps so we’re aligned:

Key points from discovery:
- Traffic spike last night caused token rate limits on Hosted API; degraded response times for customer-facing flows.
- You need predictable throughput and isolation for the transaction-processing endpoint (peak 1.2M tokens/day, sustained 350 rps at 1k-token windows).
- Compliance: currently ok with SOC2 but evaluating stricter controls; potential requirement for VPC or on-prem in Q3.

Options we discussed:
1) Stay on Hosted API with higher quotas and burst policies — fastest but still multitenant.
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) — predictable throughput, data isolation, SLA-backed latency. Typical lead time: 2–3 weeks for expedited onboarding.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full isolation, KMS/HSM integration, 4–6 weeks + security review.

Immediate ask from your team: confirm whether you want us to prepare a Dedicated expedited migration plan and SOW (recommended given the incident), or keep on Hosted and apply short-term mitigations (burst capacity, token limits).

Next steps I’ll take:
- Prepare proposed migration plan for Hosted->Dedicated (MOP + timeline + cost). Attach a sample MOP and SOW template.
- Loop in Dev (tech lead) and Neha (CS) for runbook and cutover windows.

Can you confirm the make-or-break requirements (SLA, encryption/KMS, PCI/HIPAA triggers) and whether Procurement should be looped now?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: proposed-mop-hosted-to-dedicated.pdf, SOW-dedicated-template.docx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finplus.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: capacity needs & hosted vs dedicated/private options

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Short version: the incident last night caused failures for roughly 17% of production requests for 90 minutes; customers noticed. We can’t have repeated user-facing degradation.

Priority criteria:
- Throughput & consistency > cost for next 90 days.
- Data isolation desired (not strictly mandated yet) but encryption at rest with customer-managed keys is required.
- We have a compliance review slated for mid-March — if the Dedicated route reduces risk before that, we prefer it.

Please prioritize an expedited Dedicated proposal with clear timeline and rollback plan. Procurement is copied for contracting rhythm. If Dedicated lead time is more than 10 business days we need a mitigation plan on Hosted (burst + prefix caching) while we transition.

Thanks —
Alex
Head of Product, FinPlus
alex.johnson@finplus.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finplus.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MOP & SOW — expedited technical plan and feasibility

Hi all —

Short technical summary and feasibility for expedited Dedicated migration:

Feasibility: Yes — Dedicated is a good fit for the symptoms you described. We can provision a dedicated GPU pool with the following target config:
- Target throughput: 400 rps sustained per cluster (with headroom to 600 rps)
- Memory/Quantization profile: q4_0 for cost/throughput tradeoff; we can run benchmark matrix during provisioning.

Expedited steps (details for MOP):
1) Artifact handoff: FinPlus provides model weights (if custom) or model name + tokenizer config for curated model.
2) Capacity provisioning: Request to infra team (48–72 hrs).
3) Network & KMS: For encryption with customer-managed keys, we need KMS ARN + access policy; if you want full VPC peering that’s additional 5–10 business days for networking and security review.
4) Caching & warmup: We'll import prefix cache & run synthetic traffic to warm KV cache (1 business day).
5) Cutover: Canary test (2–3 hours), then full traffic switch with rollback route.

Timeline estimate for expedited Dedicated (priority path): 6–9 business days assuming we get artifacts + KMS details day 0.

Short-term Hosted mitigations while provisioning Dedicated:
- Increase rate quota for the token bucket and enable aggressive prefix caching on the transaction endpoint (low risk).
- Deploy fallback model variant with reduced context size to lower per-request latency.

Blockers / ask from FinPlus:
- Confirm model artifact availability or specify Redwood catalog model.
- Provide KMS ARN or confirm Redwood-managed KMS for interim.
- Approve proposed maintenance window for canary (we recommend 02:00–04:00 local to your region).

I’ll attach the benchmark plan and a cron for provisioning.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
